findings.problem: Launch status stated as settled. Group 01 subject 'The Steep Club is here' and preview 'Now you can start your box' (base 01 preview too) say the Club is open; the owner has not confirmed. The body's Owner-to-confirm tag does not cover subject/preview.
findings.fix: Remove the launch claim from the subject and preview, or wrap in [Owner to confirm: ...]; use neutral wording.

findings.problem: Group 01 files are stale versus the edited base 01 (subject 'Make room for a quiet cup'); they still use the old subject.
findings.fix: Regenerate the three group 01 files from the updated base email.

findings.problem: Steeping note wording differs from the required exact line '[Owner to confirm: steeping notes come with each tea.]'. Also 'Wait the time on your card' (line 11) presents a steeping card as confirmed.
findings.fix: Use the exact required wording, and rephrase step 2 so it does not assume a card (or tag it Owner to confirm).

findings.problem: Gifting stated as fact: 'A box can be a gift' in all four 02 files; gift-buyers 02 adds 'a gift for someone who enjoys a quiet cup' and gift-buyers 03 says 'the person you give it to gets to enjoy'.
findings.fix: Wrap gifting statements in [Owner to confirm: ...].

findings.problem: Unsupported claims: 'A lot of people tell us they worry about getting tea "wrong"' (all 03 files) and 'You asked what's in the box' (all 02 files; this is a one-way send). Not backed by brand files and near the 'promises we can't keep' rule.
findings.fix: Rewrite honestly, e.g. 'If you're worried about getting tea wrong, you can't' and 'Here's what's in the box.'
